scope: All-order necessary triangle-count condition for edge-arrowing graphs, supported by independent local checks and proof audits; not a full Erdos #151 solution or categorical priority claim.

files.note: Audited threshold-six discovery report; its historical threshold-seven frontier is superseded by THRESHOLD7_LINE_GRAPH.md.

external_sources.citation: P. Hell and X. Zhu, On the adaptable chromatic number of graphs, European Journal of Combinatorics 29 (2008), 912-921, Theorem 2.1
G. Chen and G. Jing, Structural properties of edge-chromatic critical multigraphs, JCTB 139 (2019), 128-162
external_sources.use: Goldberg conjecture for maximum degree at most 39; sufficient for the 4-regular root.

external_sources.citation: G. Chen, G. Jing, and W. Zang, Proof of the Goldberg-Seymour conjecture on edge-colorings of multigraphs, JCO 50 (2025), article 23
external_sources.use: Full modern theorem; stronger alternative source.

external_sources.citation: J. Krausz, Demonstration nouvelle d'un theoreme de Whitney sur les reseaux, Mat. Fiz. Lapok 50 (1943), 75-85
external_sources.use: Classical multigraph line-graph clique-cover characterization; the proof also gives the root construction directly.

external_sources.citation: A. Bikov, Small minimal (3,3)-Ramsey graphs, arXiv:1604.03716
external_sources.use: Adjacent marked-neighbourhood framework and five-vertex local types; not the global threshold-seven closure.

trust_boundary: The threshold-seven proof is human-readable and has a separate clean-room mathematical reconstruction.
Hell-Zhu and the Goldberg edge-colouring theorem are external inputs and are not formalized here.
The local computations support but do not replace the general proof.
No independent human peer review, Lean formalization of the theorem, or exhaustive older-language priority search has occurred.
The full Erdos #151 conjecture remains open.
